Factual.content: The comment presents a narrow, dichotomous choice: "Either you take control of your government or just remain impoverished! Its either fight or starve." This confines the possibilities to two extremes—either direct political action (take control) or continued hardship—and dismisses any other courses of action (e.g., negotiation, targeted protest, or sustained civil disobedience). Such an oversimplified framing, known as a false dilemma or false dichotomy, misstates the range of viable options and therefore is a logical fallacy. The inference it actually supports is that there are only two outcomes, which is an unsupported narrowing of possibilities.

The premises are that Cubans ‘stop playing nice by uploading videos and banging pots and pans,’ leading to the conclusion that the only remaining options are to take control of the government or stay poor and starve. This forced two‑way division is a classic false dilemma.
